 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES-4603 alleging that on 15.01.2023 at 6.40 a.m. when travelling by sitting on the pillion of a motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES-4603 from Hebburu towards Kunigal prior to Kunigal Doddakere near the land owned by Gowthami, D/o. Balegowda of Balegowdapalya in the process of avoiding dashing of motorcycle to a street dog, Venkateshraju,
rider of the motorcycle rode the same negligently, applied the brake , made the motorcycle to fell,
thereby caused accident resulting in the injuries to petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Government hospital, Kunigal, Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru .
3. As on the date of accident petitioner being aged 29 years, used to earn Rs.2,00,000/per annum from agriculture and Rs.1,500/- to Rs.2,000/per day by working as bar bender 4.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Regarding accident Kunigal police registered crime No.15/2023 .

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.1, owner/ rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES-4603 appeared through his Advocate but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

6. In response to the notice respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate,
filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age, occupation,
income, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner .

7. On the basis of the pleadings on 15.07.2024 , this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 15.01.2023 at about 06.40 a.m. , on Hebbur - Kunigal road, in view of the negligent use of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-ES-4603 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?

If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
8. On 13.06.2024, 22.10.2024, petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 11 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.11.

On 08.01.2025, 12.02.2025, petitioner produced the evidence of Dr.Vivekananda B.R. as PW2 Hanumantha Raju K.N vs Venkateshraju on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121377149/
2 and produced 3 document at Exs.P.12 to P.14.

On 05.04.2025, 21.04.2025 respondent No.2 insurance company produced the evidence of Dr. Sathish Babu and officer of the insurance company as RW1 and 2 and produced 4 documents at Ex.R.1 to R.4.
9.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

10. On the basis of material available in the file, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ....
In the affirmative Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to Rs.11,99,591/-
with current and future interest at 6%p.a. on Rs.7,09,991/- from 22.10.2024 from the respondents as compensation .
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner/PW1 stated that on 15.01.2023 at 6.40 a.m. when travelling by sitting on the pillion of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES- 4603 rode by Venkateshraju from Hebburu towards Kunigal prior to Kunigal Doddakere near agriculture land owned by Gowthami, D/o. Balegowda, resident of Balegowdapalya in the process of avoiding dashing the motorcycle to the street dog, Venkateshraju, rode the motorcycle negligently, made the motorcycle along with riders to fell, thereby caused the accident , caused grievous injuries to petitioner.
12. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding reason , mode of accident.
13. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that after the accident he has been shifted to Government hospital , Kunigal in an ambulance.
PW1 admitted that Venkateshraju rider of the motorcycle never taken treatment.

Petitioner stated that after accident member of his family came to Government hospital, Kunigal and Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics,
Bengaluru.

entities.text:
Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics,
Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: PW1 denied the suggestion that on 15.01.2023 when he rode motorcycle met with an accident and suffered injuries.
PW1 submitted that Nagaraju, S/o. Lakshmanraju who was coming behind the motorcycle witnessed the accident.
PW1 denied the suggestion that he neither sitting on the pillion of motorcycle nor Venkateshraju rode the motorcycle.
PW1 denied the suggestion that by colluding with Venkateshraju and police, get fabricated documents.
14. In the evidence affidavit PW2, Dr.Vivekananda B.R. stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.
15. In the evidence RW1 Dr.Sathish Babu , General Surgeon, Community Health Center, Kunigal produced M.L.C. Extract at Ex.R.1.
RW1 stated that on 15.01.2023 intimated appearance of Hanumantharaju , S/o. Late Nagaraju with the history of RTA to SHO , Kunigal police station.

RW1 stated that in the Medico Legal Register nothing has been mentioned about appearance of Hanumantha Raju K.N vs Venkateshraju on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121377149/
3
Venkatesh Raju, S/o.Chikkamuttaraju for treatment on 15.01.2023 (page No.328 to 335).
16. In the evidence affidavit RW2 officer of insurance company reiterated the same facts as asserted in the written statement about reason and mode of accident.

17. In the evidence RW2 produced copy of the policy, letter dated 13.07.2023 sent to respondent No.1 Venkateshraju , postal acknowledgement card bearing address and signature of Venkateshraju with post office seal in which date is visible as 31.07.2023 at Exs.R.1 to R.3.
18.
In the cross-examination RW2 admitted lack of personal knowledge about the incident pertaining to the case.

19. Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR pertaining to crime No.15/2023 registered by Kunigal police on 17.01.2023 against respondent No.1 rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA- 06-ES-4603 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint presented by Nagaraju, S/o. Lakshmana Raju.
Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar.
Ex.P.3 is the Vehicle Inspection mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of Motor Vehicles Inspection Report.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of wound certificate issued by government hospital, Kunigal in which reason for the injuries are noted as RTA on 15.01.2023 at 7.00 a.m. near Kothagere, Kunigal.

Ex.P.7 is the copy of chargesheet filed by Kunigal police in crime No.15/2023 against Venkatesh Raj,
S/o. Chikka Mutturaj, rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES-4603 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
20.
In Ex.R.1 copy of MLC Register Extract appearance of Hanumantharaju, S/o. Late Nagaraju for treatment on 15.01.2023 to Government hospital , Kunigal with the history of RTA are mentioned.
In this case, respondent No.1 owner/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES-4603 neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.
21. In this case, there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 15.01.2023 at 6.40 a.m. when petitioner was travelling by sitting on the pillion of a motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES- 4603 from Hebburu towards Kunigal prior to Kunigal Doddakere near the land owned by Gowthami, D/o.

Balegowda, resident of Balegowdapalya in the process of avoiding dashing of motorcycle to the street dog, Venkateshraju, rider of the motorcycle rode the same negligently, made the motorcycle along with riders to fell, thereby caused accident , caused injuries to petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

22. Issue No.2: In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered puncture wound over anterior aspect of left leg, CLW over 2 nd WFB of left hand space, swelling W15 deformity over left thigh and leg with bony abnormal mobility over left thigh and leg , took treatment at Government hospital , Kunigal , then took treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru from 15.01.2023 to 30.01.2023, underwent surgery by spending Rs.2,50,000/-

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
PW1 stated that as on the date of accident being aged 29 years used to earn Hanumantha Raju K.N vs Venkateshraju on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121377149/
4 Rs.2,00,000/per annum by doing agriculture and Rs.1,500/- to Rs.2,000/per day by working as bar bender.
23.
In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

24. In the cross-examination PW1 denied the suggestion that in the incident neither suffered grievous injuries nor underwent surgery nor taken treatment as an inpatient but fabricated discharge summary.

PW1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of incident neither engaged in bar bending/centering/agriculture nor earning Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/p.m. PW1 stated that he does not own agricultural land .
PW1 denied the suggestion that he never spent Rs.2,50,000/- for treatment.

25. In the evidence PW2 Dr. Vivekananda stated that on 05.12.2024 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 58% to left lower limb,
which is about 19% to whole body.
In the evidence PW2 produced inpatient case sheet, OPD file and x-ray at Exs.P.12 to P.14.
26 . In the cross-examination PW2 stated that along with a team in Sanjay Gandhi hospital he treated the petitioner.
PW2 admitted that in the operation notes available in the case file his name is not mentioned.
PW2 stated that as on 12.02.2025 petitioner is under follow up treatment, as on 05.12.2024 fractures of the petitioner are united.
27. In the evidence RW1 and 2 stated nothing regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by PW1 Hanumantharaju.
28. Wound certificate.

Discharge summary , prescriptions , case file and other medical documents shows that in the accident petitioner suffered post traumatic closed left femur shaft fracture, post traumatic open type I proximal third left both bone leg fracture with no neurovascular deficits, left femur shaft fracture and proximal third left both bone leg fracture , punctured wound over anterior aspect of proximal 1/3 rd of left leg, , took treatment at Government hospital, Kunigal, then took treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru as an inpatient from 15.01.2023 to 30.01.2023.
29.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the medical records age of the petitioner is noted as 28 years.
In the copy of aadhar card marked at Ex.P.8 date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 04.04.1994.
Medical bills shows that the petitioner spent approximately Rs.46,991/- .
In the file there are no documents regarding quantum of income of the petitioner.
30. The deposition shows that as on 22.10.2024 petitioner came to Court hall by limping with the help of a walking stick and deposed by sitting on a chair.

Hence, I have inferred that in view of the injuries suffered in the accident, inspite of better treatment, petitioner suffered permanent functional disability at 15% and calculated loss of future income in the following terms:

Hanumantha Raju K.N vs Venkateshraju on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121377149/
5

Age of the petitioner Hanumantharaju as 29 years on the date of accident - Notional monthly income of the petitioner Rs.16,000/- Hanumantharaju 15%
permanent functional disability Rs.2,400/-
Loss of future income 2,400x12x17 Rs.4,89,600/-
31.

Hence, I award Rs.4.89,600/- towards loss of future income, Rs.2,00,000/- towards Pain and Sufferings, Rs.46,991/- towards treatment charges, Rs.25,000/- towards attendant , conveyance,
nourishment charges, Rs.2,88,000/- (16,000x18) towards loss of income during treatment period,
Rs.1,50,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.

32. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.11,99,591/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., on Rs.7.09.991/- from 22.10.2024 towards compensation from the respondents.

Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No.
1.
Pain and Sufferings Rs. 2,00,000-00 2.
Treatment charges Rs. 46,991-00 3. Attendant, conveyance and Rs. 25,000-00  nourishment charges 4. Loss of income during Rs. 2,88,000-00  treatment period
5. Loss of future income Rs. 4,89,600-00 6. Loss of amenities and future Rs. 1,50,000-00  unhappiness.
In the written statement , respondent No.2 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES-4603 as on the date of incident.
Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.2 shows that under policy the risk of the two persons (seating capacity 2) are covered.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident , respondent No.1 owner of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06- ES-4603 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that respondents being the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES-4603 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

Hanumantha Raju K.N vs Venkateshraju on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121377149/
6

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.11,99,591/- (Rupees eleven lakhs ninety nine thousand five hundred and ninety one only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., on Rs.7,09,991/-
from 22.10.2024 to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-ES-4603 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% of the compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.

Surplus compensation amount and interest shall be deposited in any of the bank in the name of petitioner for a period of 5 years without permitting to create any encumbrances , however, liberty is given to the petitioner to with draw interest once in 3 months.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

Bangalore.
